body.statement: Can the construction obtained from \(\mathrm{def:mixed-estimator-handle}\) be made total and computable and satisfy, for constants depending only on \(\epsilon\), \[\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{d,\epsilon}}E_{P^{\otimes n}\otimes P_{XA}^{\otimes m}}[(\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{mix}}_{n,m,d}-\tau(P))^2]\le C_\epsilon r_\epsilon(n,m,d)\] simultaneously for every \(n\ge1\), \(m\ge0\), and \(d\ge2\), with a proof that controls false-light polynomial tails, random branch means, and mass-weighted covariance summation without a factor in \(d\) or \(m/n\)?
body.justification: This isolates the first genuinely changed upper-bound step: outcome marks have budget \(n\), while unmarked factorial moments have budget \(n+m\).
body.gap: JiaoVenkatHanWeissman2015 and WuYang2016 lift every monomial factor from one sample, while ZengBalakrishnanHanKennedy2024 uses labeled four-cell counts. The finite calculation in \(\mathrm{def:finite-small-instance}\) already requires one outcome-marked factor from \(\mathcal L_n\) and a separate marginal factor from \(\mathcal U_m\); none of the comparators proves the resulting unequal-information hybrid-risk lemma.
body.consumer: The resulting estimator gives a model-free discrete benchmark for allocating chart-review outcomes in the ChengAnanthakrishnanCai2021 setting.
